newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean inflation steady at 0.3 percent in April.
newsitem.headline: Chilean inflation steady at 0.3 percent in April.

text.p: Consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in Chile last month, down from 1.0 percent in the same month of 1996 and unchanged from 0.3 percent in March this year, the National Statistics Institute said.

The figures suggested official inflation targets were on track, but analysts have warned that the inflationary effects of severe drought in central Chile are likely to be felt starting this month and in June.
The new numbers brought inflation in the first four months of the year to 2.0 percent and 6.1 percent in the 12 months through April, the institute said.

The only significant increase in consumer prices last month was in apparel, which climbed 3.0 percent. Food prices rose 0.4 percent, housing costs rose 0.3 percent and the catch-all "other" category was up 0.6 percent.
Transport and communications prices fell 0.9 percent, in keeping with seasonal patterns at the end of the summer vacation period.

President Eduardo Frei's government expects to bring Chilean inflation down to about 5.5 percent this year and four percent by the end of the decade, from 6.6 percent last year, 8.2 percent in 1995, and double digits in most of the 1980s and early 1990s.
Prices rose 8.4 percent in the 12 months to April 1996.
